posts.text:
How many people do you need in a room before two of them probably share a birthday? Just 23, the number of people on a football pitch with the referee.

With 23 people there are 253 different pairs, so the chance of a shared birthday is 50.7%. With 30 it's 70.6%, with 50 it's 97.0% and with 70 it's 99.9% (assuming 365 equally likely birthdays).

#birthdayparadox #maths #probability #statistics #truthwithdata

posts.text:
What are your real odds of winning the Lotto jackpot? Since June 2026 every £2 ticket gets two draws, which halved the odds, but they're still 1 in 22,528,738.

That's less likely than flipping 24 heads in a row, or picking one person from 250 full Wembley Stadiums. Play one line every week and you'd expect to wait about 433,000 years for a jackpot.

Play for fun, not as a plan.

#lottery #lotto #odds #maths #truthwithdata

posts.text:
Has gold beaten the Sensex? Over 33 years it's almost a tie: gold returned 11.3% a year in rupees and the Sensex 11.0% on price alone (about 12.4% with dividends).

Over the last 20 years gold clearly won, 14.4% vs 10.6%, but across every 10-year window since 1993 it won only about a third of the time. The useful part: they rarely fall together, so a 10–30% slice of gold softened the worst SIP outcomes.
